newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: POLL - Colombia voters favor ex-interior minister.
newsitem.headline: POLL - Colombia voters favor ex-interior minister.

text.p: Colombia's former interior minister Horacio Serpa has emerged as the leading candidate for next year's presidential elections in the latest poll of voter preferences published on Monday.

Serpa, who was seen as President Ernesto Samper's right hand man and is almost certain to win the official backing of the ruling Liberal Party, would take 29 percent of the vote if elections were held this week, a poll by the National Consulting Centre said.

Former chief prosecutor Alfonso Valdivieso, a favourite of Washington for his tough stance on drugs and corruption, is in second place with 22 percent. But the poll whowed he would win by six percentage points in the event of a run-off against Serpa.
A second round of voting would be held if no candidate obtained 50 percent of the vote in the first round, scheduled for May.

The poll did take into account Gen. Harold Bedoya, who was fired as head of Colombia's armed forces late last month, after months of public feuding with President Ernesto Samper over anti-guerrilla tactics.

Bedoya has said he will stand in the presidential race but has yet to formally register his candidacy. Three polls by major news organisations estimate the ousted general could win as much as 40 percent of the vote.
National Consulting Centre pollsters interviewed 1,200 Colombians over the age of 18 in 15 Colombian cities. No margin of error was given.
